Which IP to retrieve from the environment variables

Currently we have this code to retrieve an IP:
https://github.com/mirumee/saleor/blob/35d8750ae07bddb57222f5fec3512c2788b56f5c/saleor/core/utils/__init__.py#L54-L58

Which is fine–apart the fact someone can inject any else than an IP.

The question is: should we really trust the `X-Forwarded-For` header? Shouldn't we let the web server handle this part and provide us the IP it believe is correct through `REMOTE_ADDR`?

For example, in nginx, we can get the environment variable `REALIP_REMOVE_ADDR` and thus leave the choice to the user of which IP(s) and header(s) are to be **trusted** and handle the IP **validation**. With the above snippet, we don't leave the choice to the user.

Another case, is when the user has their saleor workers behind a proxy, e.g. CloudFlare. The IP would be set from `CF-Connecting-IP` to `REALIP_REMOVE_ADDR` (nginx).

I believe we could do something like this:
```python
ip_headers = ["REALIP_REMOVE_ADDR", "WHATEVER_APACHE_USES", "REMOTE_ADDR"]

for header in ip_headers:
    ip = request.META.get(header, None)
    if ip and not valid_ip(ip):
        return ip
return None
```

Metadata for Menus and Menu Items

When building/customizing storefronts for saleor, we use navigation menus in a variety of situations, some requiring additional data that is simply not built into menu items. For example, in addition to the name and link, some use cases might call for an icon or image url. Other times, you might want to mark some items as disabled or give them special styling.

When the menu item points to a collection/category, adding the metadata to the collection/category itself can sometimes be an option, but this doesn't work when the menu item is just a url. And when the menu item is updated to point to a different collection, one has to remember to set the metadata all over again.

The clear database command should be runnable with debug disabled

We should be able to run `cleardb` when `DEBUG=False` but we should have a `--force` flag to actually allow that action when the debug mode is turned off as it is a dangerous command.

Definition of done:
- Prints an error to stderr when `DEBUG=False` and `--force` is not passed (flagged)
- Exits with 1 (raises `SystemExit` which allows Django to handle it and cleanup the opened connections, such as the database)
- User can clear the database when debug mode is turned off and only when `--force` was passed
